 JUDGMENT
1. By this judgment, we shall dispose of the appeal filed by the

 Appellants against the impugned order dated 06.10.2025, passed

 by Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-VI (New Delhi), M-

 Block, 1st Floor, Vikas Bhawan, I.P. Estate, New Delhi-110002

 (hereinafter referred to as District Commission) , in Complaint Case

 no. CC-01/2021 titled as F.S. Chauhan vs. M/s Bharat Hotels Ltd.

 & Ors. inter-alia praying for setting aside the order passed by the

 District Commission.
2. While the Appellants were Opposite Parties before the District

 Commission and the Respondent was Complainant before the

 District Commission.
DISMISSED PAGE 2 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN
3. The facts of the case as per the District Forum, record are as

 under:
"1. The facts as culled out from the present complaint case
 are that the complainant negotiated for hosting of the
 wedding of his daughter at 'the Lalit' New Delhi with the
 Opposite Party No. 3 (hereinafter calledOP). For the
 purposes of rates, an agreement dated 23.07.2020 was
 finalized. However, it is alleged by the complainant that
 there were other terms unilaterally holding only the
 complainant liable for any breach and requiring him to
 give excessive security and holding him liable for the
 penalty wholly. These terms, however, have been
 protested by the complainant in this case as
 disproportionate to the possible loss amounting to 'unfair
 contract'.
2. The OP-1/hotel required a minimum guarantee of 100
 guests for lunch and 200 for dinner on 9th of December
 2020 and further, 150 for lunch and 200 for dinner on the
 10th of December 2020. The complainant was required to
 deposit Rs.27,49,400/- in advance. The banquet payment
 schedule as quoted in the complaint case, is reproduced
 below:
Banquet Payment Schedule Amount
 On signing INR 5,00,000/-
 1st Oct, 2020 INR 5,56,100/-
 1st Dec, 2020 INR 16,93,300/-
 Total INR 27,49,400/-
3. It is submitted that because of COVID period, the COVID
 Regulations as then in force, limited the number of
 persons at wedding to 50. The complainant enquired
 whether the hotel would honor the government
 regulations in force and would postpone the event for any
 unforeseen reason with full adjustment of the advance. In
 response, OP-3 promised through emails dated July 23,
 2020 that the hotel shall honor the regulations prevailing
 at the time of the event and gave a schedule of a
 contract vide email dated 28, 2020 to operate in case of
 the restriction of 50 guests, with a total consideration of
 Rs. 10,56,100/-, as under:
Room Tariff Tax Tariff Total

DISMISSED PAGE 3 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 with
 Nights tax
 50 INR 18% INR INR
 9500/- 11,210/- 5,56,500/-
Lunch INR 18% INR INR
 100 2000/- 2360/- 2,36,000/-

 Dinner INR 18% INR INR
 100 2200/- 2596/- 2,59,600/-

 Total 10,56,100/-
Further, vide email dated July 29, 2020, the OP-3
 promised to postpone the event 'for any other unforeseen
 reason'
4. On 31 July 2020, the complainant and the representative
 of OP Nos. 1 & 2 signed the contract which included the
 aforesaid emails of the OP No. 3 as its integral part. The
 complainant handed over a cheque for Rs.5,00,000/-.
5. On 1st October, 2020, the complainant handed over
 another cheque for Rs. 5,56,100/- to the representative of
 "The Lalit New Delhi". The complainant submits that a
 few days later, it was falsely purported that the cheque
 for Rs.5,56,100/- was dishonored and an excess amount
 of Rs.5,56,100/- was caused to be credited to the account
 of 'the Lalit New Delhi' and the excess amount not
 refunded despite repeated requests.
6. In the meantime the Government re-enforced the COVID
 restriction of 50 persons at the weddings w.e.f. 18th Nov.
 2020 which made it immediately imperative for the OPs
 to refund the excess amount of Rs.5,56,100/- because
 the contract amount of hosting 50 persons remained
 Rs.10,56,100/- only. It is further alleged by the
 complainant that later he came to know that the OPs sold
 the venues specified for the event to other parties for the
 same dates and made it impossible for themselves to host
 the event of the complainant. Therefore, when apprised of
 this fact in the 3rd week of November 2020 that the
 complainant himself was suffering from COVID, the OP
 No. 3 took this as an opportunity to cover the clandestine
 selling of the venues to others by postponement of his
 event so that while on one hand none for the complainant
 could come to the hotel and he without any objection
 could host the others; on the other hand, he could later

DISMISSED PAGE 4 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 allege 'No Show' against the complainant and could retain
 whole of advance. Therefore, while OP No. 3 agreed to
 'postpone' the event, he deliberately dragged on the
 finalization of the new dates and sought to let the
 scheduled dates of the event pass until when on 1st
 December 2020 he was requested to delink the refund of
 the excess amount from the finalization of the new dates
 and he suddenly became inaccessible by alleging that he
 was 'down with jaundice' and couldn't speak to his boss
 as reflected from the whatsapp chats (printout placed on
 record) of OP No. 3 from 23rd Nov. to 1st Dec.2020. The
 complainant states that on coming to know of the email
 address of his alleged boss, the complainant sent an
 email on 3rd Dec. 2020 at 4:40 pm to OP No. 3 and his
 alleged boss, i.e. OP No. 5, requiring either of them to
 finalize the new set of dates.
7. Through email dated 03.12.2020, the OP No. 5 denied
 even the postponement and asked the complainant to
 continue with the event or otherwise to lose whole of the
 advance. The complainant states at that time he was
 unaware of the sale of the venue of the event and
 inability of the OPs themselves to host the event, got
 alarmed by the denial of postponement and sought to
 clarify vide his email dated Dec. 3, 2020,
 8:15 pm that the OP No. 3 had already 'postponed' the
 event with full adjustment of the advance on the new
 date and it was merely confirmation of the venue on the
 new date which was remaining to be done and submitted
 three more sets of new dates for the event falling in
 the 'saya days' in the month of April, 2021 vide his email
 dated Dec. 4, 2020, 1:01 pm and requested him to
 confirm the availability of the venue on any one set of the
 said dates. It is stated that while, OP Nos. 3 & 5 failed to
 respond, one person named Mr. Vijay Bhalla, without any
 authority intervened to again deny the 'postponement' of
 the event and to falsely purport that the OPs were
 prepared to host the event from 9th to 11th December
 2020 even for more than 50 guests and threatened
 that if the complainant did not participate despite his
 quarantine, they would retain whole of the deposit of
 Rs.16,12,200/- vide his email dated Dec; 4, 2020 at 3:09
 pm. In further clarification, the complainant sent his own
 RT PCR Report dated Dec. 3, 2020 along with his email
 dated Dec. 4, 2020 at 5:32 pm. OP Nos. 3 & 5 again
 failed to respond and the person named above again

DISMISSED PAGE 5 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 threatened to retain the advance vide his
 email dated Dec. 4, 2020 at 9:15 pm. Suspecting the
 conduct of the OP Nos. 3 & 5, the complainant called
 upon the OP-1 to take urgent action for averting the likely
 breach of contract and violation of COVID-19
 regulations by her staff firstly by an email dated Dec. 5,
 2020 to cmdoffice@the lalit.com and further by an email
 dated Dec. 7, 2020 to corporate@the lalit.com.
8. In response, the OP-4 on behalf of the OP No. 1 Company
 vide an email dated Dec. 8, 2020 at 6:00 pm stated that
 even while they were in discussion with the complainant
 since last 15 days, they tried but could
 not get some alternate function (organized at the venue)
 and denied the postponement and asserted that the event
 as scheduled was going to be hosted the next day i.e. on
 9th December, 2020. It is further stated by the
 complainant that some of the guests, who earlier received
 the invitation cards but were not aware of the
 postponement, reported for the event at the hotel on 9th
 December, 2020 but the staff at the Reception told them
 that as per their records no such wedding event
 was ever scheduled to be held at the hotel and many of
 the banquet venues shown in the invitation card were
 already sold out to others. The guests went through huge
 embarrassment and humiliation when they saw that
 events of others were being held at the same venues and
 they had to make their own arrangement for their meals
 and accommodation at their own expense. Many of the
 guests called upon the complainant to express their
 embarrassment, humiliation and losses which they had
 to incur. Thereupon, the complainant called upon the O.P.-
 4 and other OPs to verify that events of others were being
 hosted at the same venues where they claimed to host
 the events for the complainant. This, the complainant
 submits demonstrates breach of contract, deficiency of
 services, dishonesty, and cheating.
9. The OPs could not deny the aforesaid sale of venues and
 hosting of the events of others as watched by the guests
 of the complainant. However, the OP-4, vide his email
 dated Dec. 11, 2020 at 5:13 pm, admitted only the selling
 out of the Crystal Ball Room for a wedding event to one
 Mr. Rishab Jain which Wedding event was in progress
 when he received the email of the complainant dated Dec.
 9, 2020, 10:19 pm. Yet, he declared that the advance
 amount (of Rs. 16,12,200/-) has been forfeited. Therefore,

DISMISSED PAGE 6 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 the complainant submits that apart from the commission
 of the offences punishable under sections 34/120-
 B/188/406/420 of the
Indian Penal Code
, 1860, the
 OPs in collusion with each other not only committed the
 'unfair trade practices', 'negligence', 'deficiencies in
 services' but also caused loss, injury and damages to the
 complainant, his family and guests apart from loss of his
 reputation in the eyes of large number of his friends and
 relatives as he is practicing Advocate- on-Record in the
 Supreme Court of India.
10. Since the complainant could not get his grievances
 resolved, he has filed the present complaint case before
 this Commission with the following prayers:-
(i) Direct the OPs to refund the advance deposit of
 Rs. 16,12,200/- with interest thereon @ 18% p.a.
 from 1st October, 2020 till the date of receipt/
 realization thereof;
(ii) Direct the OPs to pay a compensation of Rs. 63
 lakhs to the complainant;
(iii) Direct the OPs to pay punitive damages of Rs. 10
 lakhs for the unfair contracts and other unfair
 trade practices the Opposite Parties had
 committed and continue to be committing; and
(iv) Any other or further order be passed as deemed
 appropriate in the facts and circumstances of the
 case and in the interests of justice."
4. The District Forum after taking into consideration the material

 available on record passed the judgment dated 06.10.2025,

 whereby it held as follows:
"19. We have heard the parties and gone through the
 record. A communication/email dated 29th July, 2020
 is addressed by OP-3 to complainant wherein it is
 clearly admitted that OPs will be open to permit the
 complainant to select a different set of dates if any
 such eventuality happens due to the covid norms
 imposed by the
 Government of India. The contents of the said
 communication are reproduced below:-
"Dear Mr. Chauhan, Namaskar!

DISMISSED PAGE 7 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 As discussed, kindly note , in case due to govt
 regulation or for any other unforeseen reason, if
 the event gets postponed, the guest will be
 allowed to select a different dates as per
 availability and advance paid will be
 adjusted in full towards next event."
20. As regard payment, it is an admitted fact that the OPs
 not only got the amount demanded but got excess
 payment which was never refunded to the
 complainant. Thus, it is established that the OPs
 inspite of getting excess payment, did not block the
 venue or rooms for the wedding. From the evidence
 adduced by the complainant, it has been shown that
 the OPs sold the rooms/venue to some other party
 which fact has not been refuted by the OPs by cogent
 evidence. Contrary to what was assured by
 communication dated 29th July, 2020, the OPs by
 another communication dated 08.12.2020, refused to
 postpone the event on the grounds cited by the
 complainant.
21. Can a party accept and reject the same instrument
 taking advantage of the situation? In this connection,
 our attention has been drawn to a
 decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the
 case of 'R.N. Gasain Vs Yashpal Dhir', (2014) 15 SCC
144. The relevant paragraph is quoted below:-
"Law does not permit a person to both
 approbate and reprobate, This principle is
 based on the doctrine of election which
 postulates that no party can accept and
 reject the same instrument and that "a
 person cannot say at one time that a
 transaction is valid any thereby obtain
 some advantage, to which he could only be
 entitled on the footing that it is valid, and
 then turn round and say it is void for the
 purpose of securing some other advantage".
[See: Verschures Cremeries Ltd. V Hull and
 Netherlands Steamship Co. Ltd., (1921) 2 R.B.
 608, at p 612, Scrutton, L.J.]. According to
 Halsbury's Laws of England, 4th Edn., Vol. 16,
 "after taking an advantage under an order ( for
 example for the payment of costs) a party may

DISMISSED PAGE 8 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 be precluded from saying that it is invalid and
 asking to set it aside". (pra 1508)."
22. A three Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of
 India in the case of
'Pravasi Legal Cell v. Union of
 India
', 2020 SCC OnLine SC 799, decided
 on 01.10.2020, ordered that if a passenger has booked
 a ticket during the lockdown period (from 25th March,
 2020 to 24th May, 2020) for travel during lockdown
 period and the airline has received payment for
 booking of air ticket for travel during the same period,
 for both domestic and international air travel and the
 refund is sought by the passenger against that booking
 being cancelled, the airline shall refund the full amount
 collected without any cancellation charges. The refund
 shall be made within a period of three weeks from the
 date of cancellation.
23. After scrutiny of the documents and evidence, this
 Commission is of the view that the OPs cannot withhold
 the amount paid by the complainant as the
 complainant could not avail the facility for which
 money was paid. We do not find any fault on the part
 of the complainant keeping in mind the compelling
 circumstances due to covid-19 pandemic.
24. It is, therefore, directed that the OPs shall refund
 Rs.16,12,200 to the complainant with interest @ 9% per
 annum from the date of respective payments till
 realization, within four weeks from the date of receipt
 of this order. If the OPs fail to refund the money within
 the time stipulated, the OPs shall be liable to pay
 interest at increased rate of 12% per annum. Further
 the OPs shall pay a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- to the
 complainant as compensation for causing mental
 agony, hardship and humiliation. A sum of Rs.
 50,000/- shall be paid to the complainant towards
 litigation expenses.
With the above directions, the complaint case is
 disposed of."
5. Aggrieved by the aforesaid order of the District Forum, the

 Appellants/Opposite Parties have filed the present appeal,

 contending that the District Commission has failed to properly

 appreciate the terms and conditions of the Agreement dated

DISMISSED PAGE 9 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 23.07.2020 and the subsequent WhatsApp messages and emails

 exchanged between the parties. It is contended that the

 Complainant/Respondent himself, shortly before the scheduled

 wedding function, requested postponement of the event and also

 asked the Appellants to release the venue. The Appellants

 thereafter agreed to provide alternative dates, but the

 Complainant/respondent did not accept the same and instead

 sought refund of the amount paid.
6. It is further contended that the Agreement contained a clear

 cancellation clause providing that no refund would be payable in

 case of cancellation within the prescribed period. The Appellants

 submit that the Hotel had already blocked the rooms and banquet

 venues and had made necessary arrangements pursuant to the

 Agreement. The District Commission, according to the Appellants,

 failed to appreciate that the booking was not limited to the

 banquet or food but also included hotel rooms and other services.
7. The Appellants have also challenged the reliance placed by the.
District Commission on certain documents and medical records

 filed by the Complainant/ Respondent at a later stage, contending

 that these documents were not part of the original pleadings and

 were relied upon without giving proper opportunity to the

 Appellant to rebut the same. It is also submitted that the alleged

 COVID-related circumstances were not mentioned by the

DISMISSED PAGE 10 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 Complainant in his contemporaneous WhatsApp message or email

 dated 03.12.2020 and were subsequently relied upon to justify the

 cancellation. The Appellants further submits that Opposite Parties

 No. 2 to 5 were wrongly impleaded as parties, as the Agreement

 was entered into with Opposite Party No.1 and the other parties

 had neither received the payment nor had any independent

 contractual liability towards the Complainant.
8. It is also contended that the District Commission had failed to

 properly consider the conduct of the respondent, including the fact

 that he had himself sought postponement and release of the venue

 and subsequently did not accept the alternative dates offered by

 the Hotel. According to the Appellants, there was no deficiency in

 service or unfair trade practice on their part. The Appellant has

 also challenged the award of refund, interest, compensation for

 mental agony and litigation expenses, submitting that the same

 were not justified in the facts and circumstances of the case. It is

 contended that the respondent has failed to prove any fault,

 shortcoming or deficiency in the services provided by the

 Appellants and also failed to establish any basis for the award of

 interest at 12%. Lastly, the Appellants submit that the judgments

 relied upon by the District Commission were not applicable to the

 facts of the present case, as the rights and obligations of the

 parties were governed by the specific terms of the Agreement

DISMISSED PAGE 11 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 executed between them. Accordingly, the Appellants have prayed

 for setting aside the impugned order and dismissal of the

 complaint.
9. Reply to the appeal has been filed by the respondent, denying all

 the allegations made by the Appellant and submitting that there is

 no error in the impugned order, as the entire material available on

 record was properly scrutinized before passing the said judgment.
10. Written arguments have been filed by both the parties.
11. We have carefully considered the impugned order, the grounds of

 appeal, the written submissions and the material available on

 record.
12. The main case of the Appellants is that the Respondent himself

 requested postponement of the wedding and asked the Hotel to

 release the venue. It is also submitted that the Appellants offered

 alternative dates but the Respondent did not accept the same. The

 Appellants have, therefore, argued that they were not liable to

 refund the amount.
13. It is clear from the record that vide email dated 29.07.2020, the

 Appellants had specifically assured the Respondent that if the

 event was postponed due to Government restrictions or any other

 unforeseen reason, he would be allowed to select another date,

 subject to availability, and the advance amount already paid would

 be adjusted in full towards the next event. This assurance formed

DISMISSED PAGE 12 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 part of the arrangement between the parties and was rightly

 considered by the learned District Commission.
14. It is also not in dispute that the wedding was scheduled during the

 COVID-19 period when restrictions were in force. The Respondent

 had requested postponement of the event in view of the prevailing

 circumstances. Therefore, his request for postponement cannot be

 treated as an ordinary cancellation of the booking.
15. The Appellants have relied upon the cancellation clause of the

 Agreement and have argued that the amount could be forfeited.

 However, the said clause cannot be considered separately from the

 assurance given by the Appellants regarding postponement of the

 event and adjustment of the advance amount. The terms of the

 Agreement have to be read as a whole.
16. The learned District Commission has rightly noticed that although

 the Appellants had received the amount from the Respondent, the

 venue and rooms were not kept available for his wedding. The

 record further shows that the Crystal Ballroom was made available

 to another party for a wedding event. Thus, the Respondent was

 ultimately not able to avail the services for which he had paid the

 amount.
17. The contention of the Appellants that the Respondent himself

 released the venue also does not help them. The correspondence

 between the parties shows that the Respondent was seeking

DISMISSED PAGE 13 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 postponement and was asking the Hotel to confirm alternative

 dates. He had also suggested different dates. Therefore, the

 request for postponement cannot be treated as a final and

 unconditional cancellation of the booking.
18. The Appellants have also argued that the Respondent

 subsequently relied upon medical documents relating to COVID

 and that such documents were not mentioned in his earlier

 correspondence. However, the fact remains that the dispute arose

 during the COVID-19 period and the request for postponement

 was made in the background of the restrictions prevailing at that

 time. The learned District Commission has considered the

 correspondence and other material available on record and has

 reached a reasoned conclusion.
19. We also do not find merit in the contention that the learned

 District Commission ignored the Agreement between the parties.

 On the contrary, the impugned order shows that the learned

 District Commission considered the Agreement as well as the

 subsequent communication dated 29.07.2020. The specific

 assurance given by the Appellants regarding postponement and

 adjustment of the advance amount was an important part of the

 arrangement between the parties.
20. In our view, the Appellants cannot, on the one hand, assure the

 Respondent that the event could be postponed and that the

DISMISSED PAGE 14 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 advance would be adjusted towards the next event and, on the

 other hand, subsequently refuse the postponement and retain the

 entire amount. The learned District Commission has rightly

 considered the conduct of the Appellants in this regard.
21. The Appellants have further submitted that there was no

 deficiency in service on their part. The Appellants had received the

 amount from the Respondent for providing the booked hotel and

 banquet services. However, the Respondent was ultimately unable

 to avail those services, and the venue was made available to

 another party. In these circumstances, the finding of deficiency in

 service recorded by the learned District Commission is justified.
22. As regards the refund of Rs.16,12,200/-, we find that the same

 was rightly directed to be refunded. The Appellants have not been

 able to show any sufficient reason for retaining the entire amount

 when the Respondent did not receive the services for which the

 payment was made.
23. We also find no reason to interfere with the compensation of

 Rs.1,00,000/- awarded by the learned District Commission. The

 Respondent had made arrangements for the wedding of his

 daughter and the failure to provide the booked venue and services

 caused him hardship and inconvenience. The compensation

 awarded by the learned District Commission cannot be said to be

 excessive.
DISMISSED PAGE 15 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN
24. Similarly, the amount of Rs.50,000/- awarded towards litigation

 expenses also does not call for interference, as the Respondent was

 required to approach the Consumer Commission for recovery of

 the amount which was withheld by the Appellants.
25. The learned District Commission has awarded interest @ 9% per

 annum from the respective dates of payment till realization, with a

 higher rate of 12% per annum only in case the Appellants fail to

 comply with the order within the stipulated period. We find no

 sufficient ground to interfere with the said direction.
26. The contention regarding the judgments relied upon by the learned

 District Commission also does not require any interference. The

 learned District Commission considered the peculiar facts of the

 present case, particularly the COVID-19 restrictions, the

 assurance given by the Appellants and the subsequent conduct of

 the parties.
27. We have also considered the other grounds raised by the

 Appellants, including the objection regarding the filing of

 documents at a later stage and the impleadment of Opposite

 Parties No. 2 to 5. However, the Appellants have not been able to

 show that any such ground causes any material error in the

 impugned order or changes the basic facts of the case.
28. On overall consideration of the matter, we find that the learned

 District Commission has rightly appreciated the facts and evidence

DISMISSED PAGE 16 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
 BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN

 available on record. The findings recorded by the learned District

 Commission are supported by the correspondence between the

 parties and the circumstances prevailing at the relevant time.
29. The Appellants have failed to show any illegality, infirmity or error

 in the impugned order which would require interference by this

 Commission. The grounds raised in the appeal are mainly based

 on the same facts which were already considered by the learned

 District Commission.
30. In view of the above discussion, we are of the considered view that

 the impugned order dated 06.10.2025 passed by the learned

 District Commission is based on proper appreciation of the

 material available on record and is legally justified. We find no

 reason to take a different view.
31. Accordingly, the present appeal is dismissed. The impugned order

 dated 06.10.2025 passed by the learned District Commission in

 Complaint Case No.01/2021 is upheld. There shall be no order as

 to costs.
32. The Appellants shall comply with the directions contained in the

 impugned order within the period prescribed therein.
33. Application(s) pending, if any, stand disposed of in terms of the

 aforesaid judgment.
34. The judgment be uploaded forthwith on the website of the

 Commission for the perusal of the parties.
DISMISSED PAGE 17 OF 18
 FA-544/2025 D.O.D:31.08.2026
BHARAT HOTELS LTD. & ORS. VS. F.S. CHAUHAN
35. File be consigned to record room along with a copy of this

 Judgment.
JUSTICE SANGITA DHINGRA SEHGAL
 (PRESIDENT)

DISMISSED PAGE 18 OF 18
